articles.title: Synthetic CBD derivative prevents seizures in mice without causing sedation
articles.summary: A newly synthesized version of CBD protects mice against severe seizures without causing sedation. The compound also helps normalize the growth of brain cell connections, offering a potential new avenue for treating developmental epilepsy syndromes.

articles.title: Public treats risks for low intelligence and heart disease similarly when selecting embryos
articles.summary: A new study in Nature Human Behaviour reveals that 61 percent of people are willing to screen embryos for non-medical traits. When making concrete choices, participants avoided statistical risks for low IQ just as strongly as heart disease.

articles.title: LLMs or Naive Bayes? Old Gems or New Ways
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.13185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) prompt a recurring question in research computing: should classical methods like Naive Bayes (NB) be retired? We benchmark Complement Naive Bayes against zero-shot and few-shot LLMs spanning four model families and a 37x range in scale (27B to a 1T-parameter mixture-of-experts) across text classification tasks. LLMs dominate only in zero-data regimes (98.0% vs 88.2% on Amazon Polarity sentiment), and even that win is contamination-prone: on a low-contamination sentiment task NB beats the zero-shot LLM (81.7% vs 73.0%)

articles.title: New study challenges the core assumption behind the world’s most widely used implicit bias test
articles.summary: A new study analyzing over 100,000 test sessions suggests the popular Implicit Association Test is driven more by a person's conscious effort to avoid mistakes than by their automatic, unconscious prejudices.

articles.title: Smelling chocolate helped men complete more reps without feeling more tired
articles.summary: Simply smelling chocolate helped men complete more leg extension repetitions without making the workout feel harder, with dark chocolate producing the strongest effect. The researchers think familiar food aromas may influence appetite and motivation by making the brain anticipate eating.

articles.title: Scientists discover a major brain shift between ages 50 and 75
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered sweeping changes in how the human brain controls and organizes its genome beginning in midlife, offering new clues to why aging sharply increases the risk of Alzheimer’s and other neurodegenerative diseases. One of the biggest shifts occurred between about ages 50 and 75, when many of the brain’s original immune cells declined and were replaced by cells with more inflammatory characteristics. Researchers also found weakening of cells that help maintain the blood-brain barrier, along with widespread deterioration in the genome’s three-dimensional organization.

articles.title: Common antidepressants might help liver cells clear a dangerous type of cholesterol
articles.summary: Common antidepressants might offer an unexpected benefit by helping liver cells absorb and clear a stubborn, disease-causing type of cholesterol. This cellular discovery could eventually lead to dual-purpose treatments for patients facing both depression and cardiovascular risks.

articles.title: Massive study of over a million people identifies hundreds of genetic variants linked to personality
articles.summary: A massive genetic analysis of over a million people has identified hundreds of specific DNA variations tied to human personality. The findings suggest the genetic basis of personality is highly consistent and independent of a person's family environment.

articles.title: A child’s genetic profile for ADHD can predict their parents’ risk of separation
articles.summary: A child's genetic likelihood for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder is associated with a higher chance of their parents divorcing. The new findings highlight how children might actively shape the life trajectories of their families.

articles.title: Universal two-child policy linked to increased depression among Chinese women
articles.summary: When China relaxed its family planning rules to allow all couples to have two children, depressive symptoms unexpectedly rose among married women. A new study reveals how financial constraints and family pressures contributed to this psychological toll.

articles.title: Hidden brain wiring may help keep the mind sharp as gray matter shrinks
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that the brain’s short-range wiring may help protect cognition even as gray matter shrinks with age. Healthier connections just beneath the brain’s surface were linked to better language skills and appeared to weaken the impact of gray matter loss.
